title: What Is The Interval | Piano Guessing Game #musictheory
description:
In this piano interval quiz, I play one note on the piano while hiding the second note, and the on-screen text asks a simple but powerful question what is the interval 

Watch my free online painless piano masterclass https//helenaun.com/masterclass-registration 

This ear training challenge is designed to test your music theory knowledge, interval recognition, and piano listening skills in a quick and interactive way. 

By hearing a single played note and identifying the distance to the hidden note, you actively train your relative pitch and improve your ability to recognize note relationships on the keyboard. 

Interval training is one of the most essential skills for pianists, musicians, and music students because it helps with playing piano by ear, building chords, understanding harmony, improvisation, and transcription. 

Whether you are a beginner learning piano fundamentals or an advanced player refining your ear, practicing intervals like major thirds, minor thirds, perfect fifths, fourths, sixths, sevenths, and octaves strengthens your overall musicianship. 

Hidden note exercises and piano ear training quizzes like this are widely used in piano lessons and music education to make learning music theory engaging and practical instead of purely theoretical. 

As you replay the note and visualize the keyboard, your brain learns to connect pitch distance with finger placement, improving sight-reading, composition, and improvisation skills. 

If you enjoy piano challenges, note guessing games, and interval identification tests, this quick piano quiz is a fun way to sharpen your ears daily. 

Comment your answer, test your listening accuracy, and keep practicing interval recognition to become more confident at identifying piano intervals instantly and playing music by ear with greater accuracy.

title: Cmaj7 and C7 Are NOT The Same Chord
description:
Cmaj7 and C7 might look almost identical on paper, but they do completely different jobs in music.

The secret?

One note changes.

Cmaj7 contains a B natural.

C7 contains a B♭.

That single note changes the sound, the tension, and even the function of the chord.

In this lesson you'll learn:

• How to build a Cmaj7 chord

• How to build a C7 chord

• The difference between a major 7 and a dominant 7

• Why Cmaj7 sounds smooth and colorful

• Why C7 creates tension and wants to resolve

• How C7 naturally pulls to F major

Remember:

Cmaj7 = C E G B

C7 = C E G B♭

One note changed.

Everything changed.

Lesson 5 of the GCH Guitar Academy fingerstyle guitar course, how to play alternating bass lines and how to play the guitar tune 'Just a ditty' by Sad Fantasy

https://www.ebooks4guitar.com/fingerstyle-guitar.htm

Fingerpicking or fingerstyle guitar is used in virtually all styles of music and therefore is really useful to learn.  Whilst fingerpicking guitar is most associated with acoustic guitar you don't need to learn fingerpicking guitar on an acoustic guitar as it can sound just as good on an electric guitar.  Fingerstyle guitar is used in classical guitar, folk, bluegrass, rock, blues, jazz and virtually any style of guitar you can mention.

This is a series of carefully designed progressive guitar lessons that will carry you through from an absolute beginner on the guitar to a good level of proficiency in fingerstyle guitar.  The GCH Guitar Academy guitar lessons are published to YouTube on a weekly basis just as if you were having private guitar lessons but with the advantage of having the guitar lessons exactly when and where you want them.  This gives you time to practice the lessons on your guitar between lessons so that you get the most from each guitar tutorial and achieve your goals as a guitar player.

You will need some basic knowledge of guitar chords to do this course and basic knowledge of how to read guitar tablature so therefore I recommend you view the following 2 videos before starting on this guitar course.

title: Can’t Find My Way Home - The Secret! Easy Guitar Lesson
description:
How to play Can't Find My Way Home by Blind Faith on guitar.

This beautiful acoustic classic has intimidated guitar players for decades, but it's actually much easier than most people think once you understand the secret behind the chord shapes and picking pattern.

Many players first discovered the song through the famous fireside performance by Steve Winwood, where he effortlessly brings the song to life with nothing more than an acoustic guitar and his voice. The good news is that the guitar part is built on a few simple ideas that repeat throughout the song.

In this lesson, I'll show you the secret, the strumming version, the picking version, and how everything fits together so you can start playing this classic song right away.

A great one to work on if you want to improve your acoustic playing, learn a timeless classic, and add a song to your repertoire that sounds much harder than it really is.

title: Building a 'Financial House' - the personal finance basics for expats
description:
In this video, I explain financial planning using a simple house metaphor that makes everything much clearer.
Think of your finances as building a strong house:

The Foundation → Emergency fund, health insurance & life insurance for those who need it (the most important base)
The Walls → Your retirement plan (what supports your long-term security)
The Roof → Bigger goals like saving for a house deposit or children’s education
The Garden → Adventurous investments such as stocks and crypto (nice to have, but not the main structure)

Whether you’re new to financial planning or already have some pieces in place, this framework helps expats in China understand what to prioritise and in what order.
If you’re living in China as an expat and want to build wealth with clarity and confidence, this video is for you.

title: 7 Weird Money Habits That Are Secretly Genius
description:
Most people think building wealth means cutting lattes and budgeting harder. They're wrong.
In this video, I run the actual math on 7 counterintuitive money habits — including why investing while in debt can net you $39,200 more.
🔢 The numbers will surprise you.

Two people. Same salary. Same starting point.
10 years later — one has $310,000. The other has $41,000.
The difference isn't income. It's which smart money habits they used.

The one with $310,000 did things that looked financially irresponsible:
invested while carrying debt, didn't pay off the mortgage early, drove 
a 3-year-old used car, and never actively managed a single investment.

The "responsible" one followed every rule. Saved first. Paid off debt.
Waited until everything was in order before investing.

The math tells a different story.

In this video, I break down 7 financial habits that look completely wrong 
— until you run the actual numbers. You'll see why delaying investment 
by just 2 years costs $247,000 at retirement. Why one new car purchase 
silently drains $163,000 from your future. And why the wealthiest 
Americans automate their money at nearly twice the rate of average earners.

These aren't opinions. Every number in this video comes from JP Morgan, 
Vanguard, Edmunds, DALBAR, and the Federal Reserve.

This is the math they never taught you.

Step 3: The Bottom Fill – Fixing dark occlusion edges and smoothing the jawline.
Step 4: The Rim Light – Adding a "kicker" to separate your subject and add 3D depth.
Whether you're new to Redshift or looking to refine your 3D portrait workflow, these lighting secrets will help you elevate your renders to a professional level.
